headline: Google's five-language ADK exposes tools through different runtime safeguards

source.title: One Agent Development Kit, five languages

read_evidence.scope: Entire developer article, the MCP/A2A shared interoperability architecture and original per-language examples across Python signature inference, Go struct/generics graph workflows, TypeScript Zod, Java schema annotations, Kotlin compile-time KSP and evaluation.

reading_estimation_basis.source_word_count_method: original publisher article main-text editorial estimate

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Editorial approximation, not measured reader session

summary: Google describes native Agent Development Kit implementations for Python, Go, TypeScript, Java and Kotlin. All support MCP tool connections and A2A agent communication, but their tool schemas are built differently: Python introspection, Go generics, TypeScript Zod, Java annotations and Kotlin compilation. The examples expose interoperability choices rather than proving identical production behavior.
why_it_matters: Teams can build agents in their established runtime instead of adding a Python service solely for orchestration. Compare schema validation, traceability, deployment and protocol interoperability with the same test tool before adopting a language-specific implementation.
related_coverage: See companion October 14 coverage for engineering, responsible tasks, knowledge context and safe skills.
image_alt_intent: Five language-native tool schema mechanisms converging into shared MCP tool exchange and A2A agent messaging; distinct build-time and runtime schema validation stages and evaluation lanes.
